title: SecHelix secret lifecycle record v1
description: The remediation state of one exposed credential, from detection through revocation, rotation, per-surface cleanup and retest. Detection alone is not a state. The record never carries the secret's value: a sighting is reduced at the door to a truncated SHA-256 fingerprint so two sightings can be correlated without either storing the credential.

secret.description: The credential, named by fingerprint. There is no property here for the value, and adding one would be the defect this schema exists to prevent.

fingerprint.description: Truncated SHA-256 over a domain-separated encoding of the value. Correlates sightings; it is not a confidentiality control for a low-entropy secret.

kind.description: What sort of credential this is, as classified by the detector. Free text: the taxonomy of credential shapes is open.

state.description: UNKNOWN is the default and is never a synonym for remediated. REMEDIATED requires confirmed revocation, every located surface cleared by an action that clears that surface, no unsearched surface, and a retest showing the old credential is rejected.

surfaces.description: All seven surfaces, always. A surface omitted from a report reads as clean; a surface present with NOT_SEARCHED reads as what it is.

revocation.description: Invalidating the credential at the issuer. The only step whose reach extends to copies that have already left.

rotation.description: Issuing a replacement. Restores the service and does nothing to the leaked credential, which is why it is recorded separately from revocation and never satisfies it.

assertion.description: What the retest asserted, e.g. that the old credential is rejected by the issuer.

confirmed_steps.description: Steps that completed with evidence. A claim is not a completion and does not appear here.

blockers.description: Every reason REMEDIATED is withheld, stated so the reader sees what is outstanding rather than a bare status.

status.description: CONFIRMED requires evidence. CLAIMED exists so an unevidenced assertion is recorded as one rather than rounded up.
NOT_SEARCHED is the default and means unknown, not clean.

accepted_cleanup_actions.description: The actions that clear this surface. The sets are disjoint across surfaces: REMOVED_FROM_SOURCE appears only under SOURCE, so deleting a secret from the working tree can never be recorded as the fix for git history.

residual_note.description: What a cleanup of this surface still does not reach. Present on every surface so 'cleaned' is never read as 'recalled'.
